description: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 against the working tree. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/nusselt_number_correlations/input_structs.rs, WakaoData::get() (~line 178-192) computes Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Re^0.3333 * Pr^0.6 (c=0.3333333333 applied to reynolds, d=0.6 applied to prandtl). The published Wakao correlation (Wakao & Funazkri 1978 for Sherwood; Wakao, Kaguei & Funazkri 1979 heat-transfer analogue, the form cited in the struct's own doc comment) is Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Pr^(1/3) * Re^0.6 -- the exponents on Re and Pr are SWAPPED in the code. The doc comment 'Nu = 2.0 + 1.1 * Re^0.333 Pr^0.6' faithfully describes the wrong code. Magnitude: at Re=4000, Pr=0.66 (helium in an HTR-10-like bed) the correct form gives Nu ~= 141, the as-coded form ~= 16 -- roughly a factor 9 under-prediction of particle-to-fluid heat transfer. Any packed-bed component using WakaoData inherits this. Found while building the HTR-10 pebble-bed CHT layer (op-jyyp.5); tampines/src/pebble_bed/cht.rs implements the correct form and carries a documented-discrepancy test referencing this bead. Fix in TUAS + audit callers; not fixed by the pebble-bed agent because TUAS ownership was scoped to the solid database only.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: Fixed and pushed 2026-08-11 in commit e0f0568a on develop. WakaoData::get now computes Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Pr^(1/3) * Re^0.6, with the 1979 Nusselt-form citation added alongside the 1978 Sherwood one (the doc comment previously cited only the mass-transfer paper while implementing the heat-transfer form). +196 lines of tests; cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib nusselt -> 14 passed, 0 failed, 103.67 s. Downstream follow-ups remain open and are NOT covered by this fix: op-fsk9 (the pre-fix baseline was never measured, so calibration masking is unresolved), op-29s8 (stale 'defect still current' notes in tampines pebble_bed), op-lmye (CIET heater v2 feeds hydraulic-diameter Reynolds into a particle-diameter correlation), op-fv5f (other op-4542 audit mismatches).

title: tuas: Wakao packed-bed Nusselt has Re and Pr exponents swapped

description:
s13 and s14. A Kovan artifact is: a Markdown heading immediately followed by a fenced `toml` block containing [kovan]. No bespoke Markdown syntax, no HTML comments. Ordinary TOML fences WITHOUT [kovan] remain ordinary code examples and must be left alone.

Mandatory schema: [kovan] id, kind, created, modified. Optional: reviewed. Initial kind vocabulary, deliberately small until dogfooding proves more: note, annotation, source_reference, formula, digitised_table, digitised_graph.

DO NOT try to evolve src/project.rs's SECTION_ORDER into this. That is a closed set of 6 sections (ai_summary, author_summary, full_text, table_csvs, graph_csvs, annotations) addressed by REGENERATED LINE RANGES, invalidated by every edit; this is an OPEN set of artifacts addressed by STABLE IDS (s40). Different models. Build alongside, keep project.rs's 8 tests green, and migrate.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: DEPENDENCY CORRECTED 2026-08-31: this bead was originally wired to depend on op-9vo6.5 (paper directory + citekey-as-id), which transitively made it wait on op-k25f (kopitiam-bibliography). That was over-constrained. The fenced-TOML artifact parser is a pure text -> struct transformation -- it recognises 'a markdown heading immediately followed by a fenced toml block containing [kovan]' and validates the mandatory id/kind/created/modified schema. None of that needs a BibTeX parser or a citekey: s15 explicitly says the source document is IMPLICIT from the containing paper directory and the citekey is NOT repeated on every artifact. Fully testable against synthetic markdown fixtures with no paper directory in existence. Unblocking it also unblocks op-9vo6.13/.14/.15 for earlier start.

title: kovan redesign 12: fenced-TOML artifact parser

description:
Maintainer report, 2026-08-14: the control-rod insertion slider in htgr_sim_v1's operator panel (panels.rs, drives PlantCommands::control_rod_insertion_fraction) is too sensitive -- small mouse movements produce large reactivity swings.

Likely candidates to check before picking a fix: (a) the slider's egui::Slider range/step is too coarse relative to the 0.0-1.0 insertion-fraction domain -- consider a finer drag-speed or a logarithmic/non-linear response near the operating point; (b) the rod worth curve (teh-o-prke::control_rod_feedback::obtain_rod_worth_cylinder, the Lamarsh S-curve) is steepest near mid-insertion by construction, so a linear slider naturally feels most sensitive there -- this may be physically correct and the fix may be UI-only (finer drag granularity / a numeric entry box alongside the slider), not a physics change.

Do not silently change the S-curve response to fix a UI-sensitivity complaint -- confirm which one is at fault first.
title: htgr_sim_v1: control-rod insertion slider is too sensitive
